title: Weigh it, Pour it: Weight and Capacity

standard_text: Measurement of weight (kg, g) and capacity (L, mL): estimating, measuring, converting and solving problems (summary of NCERT Maths Mela Class 4)
meta_desc: Class 4 Weigh it, Pour it worksheet (Maths Mela Chapter 8): kg and g, L and mL, scales, jugs, converting and problems. 100 questions with answers.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Weight: 1 kg = 1,000 g. Capacity: 1 L = 1,000 mL.
  • Find what each small mark on a scale is worth before reading it.

Examples

Example

Write 2 kg 350 g in grams.

2,000 + 350

Answer: 2,350 g

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Using 100 g = 1 kg1,000 g make 1 kg.
Reading the scale at the wrong markCount the value of each small step.

faq.q: How many millilitres are in a litre?

faq.a: How heavy something is, measured in grams and kilograms.

items.q: How many grams are in half a kilogram?
items.e: 1 kg = 1,000 g. Half of 1,000 is 500, so half a kilogram is 500 g.

items.q: The kitchen scales show the mass of a bunch of grapes. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 200 g. There are 4 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 200 g ÷ 4 = 50 g. Count the spaces after 200 g: 250 g. So it is 250 g.

items.q: The kitchen scales show the mass of a bag of potatoes. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 200 g. There are 4 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 200 g ÷ 4 = 50 g. Count the spaces after 600 g: 650 g. So it is 650 g.

items.q: The kitchen scales show the mass of a tub of yoghurt. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 200 g. There are 4 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 200 g ÷ 4 = 50 g. Count the spaces after 800 g: 850 g. So it is 850 g.

items.q: The kitchen scales show the mass of a block of cheese. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 250 g. There are 5 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 250 g ÷ 5 = 50 g. Count the spaces after 250 g: 300 g, 350 g. So it is 350 g.

items.q: The kitchen scales show the mass of a bag of rice. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 250 g. There are 5 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 250 g ÷ 5 = 50 g. Count the spaces after 500 g: 550 g, 600 g. So it is 600 g.

items.q: The kitchen scales show the mass of a bag of oranges. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 250 g. There are 5 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 250 g ÷ 5 = 50 g. Count the spaces after 750 g: 800 g, 850 g, 900 g. So it is 900 g.

items.q: The kitchen scales show the mass of a pineapple. What is the mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 500 g. There are 5 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 500 g ÷ 5 = 100 g. Count the spaces after 1,000 g: 1,100 g, 1,200 g, 1,300 g. So it is 1,300 g.

items.q: The needle is halfway between two marks. What is the mass of the bag of flour?
items.e: Each mark is 200 ÷ 2 = 100 g. The needle is halfway between 400 g and 500 g. Halfway between them is 450 g.

items.q: The scales show the mass of a bag of potting mix. What is the mass?
items.e: Each kilogram is split into 4 spaces, so each mark is 1,000 ÷ 4 = 250 g. The needle is 3 marks past 2 kg: 3 × 250 = 750 g. So it is 2 kg 750 g.

items.q: The scales show the mass of a watermelon. What is the mass?
items.e: Each kilogram is split into 2 spaces, so each mark is 1,000 ÷ 2 = 500 g. The needle is 1 mark past 3 kg: 1 × 500 = 500 g. So it is 3 kg 500 g.
Each kilogram is split into 10 spaces, so each mark is 1,000 ÷ 10 = 100 g. The needle is 8 marks past 1 kg: 8 × 100 = 800 g. So it is 1 kg 800 g.

items.q: The scales show the mass of a bag of dog food. What is the mass?
items.e: Each kilogram is split into 4 spaces, so each mark is 1,000 ÷ 4 = 250 g. The needle is 1 mark past 4 kg: 1 × 250 = 250 g. So it is 4 kg 250 g.
Each kilogram is split into 10 spaces, so each mark is 1,000 ÷ 10 = 100 g. The needle is 6 marks past 2 kg: 6 × 100 = 600 g. So it is 2 kg 600 g.

items.q: Varun stands on the bathroom scales. What is his mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 5 kg. There are 5 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 5 kg ÷ 5 = 1 kg. Count the spaces after 30 kg: 31 kg, 32 kg, 33 kg. So it is 33 kg.

items.q: Neha stands on the bathroom scales. What is her mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 10 kg. There are 5 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 10 kg ÷ 5 = 2 kg. Count the spaces after 30 kg: 32 kg, 34 kg, 36 kg. So it is 36 kg.

items.q: Mother stands on the bathroom scales. What is her mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 20 kg. There are 4 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 20 kg ÷ 4 = 5 kg. Count the spaces after 40 kg: 45 kg, 50 kg, 55 kg. So it is 55 kg.

items.q: Karan stands on the bathroom scales. What is his mass?
items.e: The numbers go up by 10 kg. There are 10 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 10 kg ÷ 10 = 1 kg. Count the spaces after 20 kg: 21 kg, 22 kg, 23 kg, 24 kg, 25 kg, 26 kg, 27 kg. So it is 27 kg.

items.q: Isha stands on the bathroom scales. What is her mass?
items.e: From 30 kg to 35 kg there are 10 spaces, so each mark is 5,000 g ÷ 10 = 500 g, not 1 kg. The pointer is 5 marks past 30 kg: 5 × 500 g = 2,500 g = 2 kg 500 g. 30 kg + 2 kg 500 g = 32 kg 500 g.

items.q: Kitchen scales have a mark every 250 g. The needle is 3 marks past 1 kg. What is the mass?
items.e: Each mark is 250 g, not 1 g. 3 marks: 250, 500, 750. So it is 1 kg 750 g.

items.q: A jug has a line every 250 mL. How many spaces are there from 0 up to 1 L?
items.e: 1 L = 1,000 mL. Count by 250: 250, 500, 750, 1,000. That is 4 spaces. Do not count the 0 line as a space.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers go up by 200 mL. There are 4 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 200 mL ÷ 4 = 50 mL. Count the spaces after 200 mL: 250 mL, 300 mL, 350 mL. So it is 350 mL.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers go up by 200 mL. There are 4 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 200 mL ÷ 4 = 50 mL. Count the spaces after 600 mL: 650 mL. So it is 650 mL.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers go up by 250 mL. There are 5 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 250 mL ÷ 5 = 50 mL. Count the spaces after 250 mL: 300 mL, 350 mL, 400 mL. So it is 400 mL.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers go up by 250 mL. There are 5 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 250 mL ÷ 5 = 50 mL. Count the spaces after 750 mL: 800 mL, 850 mL. So it is 850 mL.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers go up by 100 mL. There are 4 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 100 mL ÷ 4 = 25 mL. Count the spaces after 100 mL: 125 mL, 150 mL, 175 mL. So it is 175 mL.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers go up by 100 mL. There are 4 spaces between two numbers, so each mark is 100 mL ÷ 4 = 25 mL. Count the spaces after 300 mL: 325 mL. So it is 325 mL.

items.q: The water is halfway between two lines. How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers go up by 200 mL with 2 spaces, so each line is 100 mL. The water is halfway between 500 mL and 600 mL. Halfway is 550 mL.

items.q: The water is halfway between two lines. How much water is in the jug?
items.e: The numbers go up by 200 mL with 2 spaces, so each line is 100 mL. The water is halfway between 200 mL and 300 mL. Halfway is 250 mL.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: Each litre is split into 4 spaces, so each line is 1,000 ÷ 4 = 250 mL. The water is 1 line above 1 L: 1 × 250 = 250 mL. So it is 1 L 250 mL.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: Each litre is split into 4 spaces, so each line is 1,000 ÷ 4 = 250 mL. The water is 3 lines above 1 L: 3 × 250 = 750 mL. So it is 1 L 750 mL.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: Each litre is split into 10 spaces, so each line is 1,000 ÷ 10 = 100 mL. The water is 4 lines above 1 L: 4 × 100 = 400 mL. So it is 1 L 400 mL.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: Each litre is split into 2 spaces, so each line is 1,000 ÷ 2 = 500 mL. The water is 1 line above 2 L: 1 × 500 = 500 mL. So it is 2 L 500 mL.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: Each litre is split into 4 spaces, so each line is 1,000 ÷ 4 = 250 mL. The water is 3 lines above 2 L: 3 × 250 = 750 mL. So it is 2 L 750 mL.

items.q: How much water is in the jug?
items.e: Each litre is split into 5 spaces, so each line is 1,000 ÷ 5 = 200 mL. The water is 3 lines up from the bottom: 3 × 200 = 600 mL. It has not reached 1 L.

items.q: How much more water is needed to fill the jug to 2 L?
items.e: Each line is 250 mL, so the water is at 1 L 750 mL. One more line reaches 2 L. So 250 mL more is needed.

items.q: Rehan pours in 150 mL more water. How much water will be in the jug?
items.e: Each line is 50 mL, so the water is at 350 mL now. Pouring in means add: 350 + 150 = 500 mL.

items.q: Which amount is the same as 1,500 mL?
A jug has lines every 250 mL. The water is halfway between the 500 mL line and the 1 L line. How much water is in the jug?
items.e: From 500 mL to 1,000 mL is 500 mL. Half of 500 is 250. 500 + 250 = 750 mL.

items.q: A jug has a line every 100 mL. The water is 4 lines above 1 L. How much water is in the jug?
items.e: Each line is 100 mL, not 1 mL. 4 × 100 = 400 mL. So it is 1 L 400 mL.
1,000 g = 1 kg, so 5,000 g is 5 groups of 1,000 g: 5 kg.
1,000 g = 1 kg. How many groups of 1,000 are in 7,000? 7,000 ÷ 1,000 = 7, so it is 7 kg.
1,000 g = 1 kg. How many groups of 1,000 are in 3,000? 3,000 ÷ 1,000 = 3, so it is 3 kg.

items.q: Which is heavier: 3 kg or 2,500 g?
items.e: 3 kg = 3,000 g. 3,000 g is more than 2,500 g, so 3 kg is heavier.

items.q: Which is heavier: 1 kg or 900 g?
items.e: Change to the same unit: 1 kg = 1,000 g. 1,000 g is more than 900 g, so 1 kg is heavier. A bigger number is not always more.

items.q: 2 kg = ☐ g
Look at the pan balance. Which object is lighter?
items.e: The pan with the jar of jam is lower, so the jar is heavier and the beach ball is lighter. The beach ball is big, but it is full of air.

items.q: Half of a kilogram is how many grams?
items.e: 1 kg = 1,000 g. Half of 1,000 is 500, so half a kilogram is 500 g. (50 g would be half of 100 g.)

items.q: Which fact about mass is true?
items.e: Kilo means 1,000. One kilogram is 1,000 grams.

items.q: Look at the pan balance. Which object is heavier?
items.e: The pan with the brick is lower, so the brick is heavier. The pillow is bigger, but a bigger object is not always heavier.

items.q: 5 kg = ☐ g
10 kg = ☐ g
2 kg 400 g = ☐ g
3 kg 50 g = ☐ g
items.e: 3 kg = 3,000 g. Add the 50 g: 3,000 + 50 = 3,050 g. Writing 3,500 g would add 500 g, not 50 g.
1.5 kg is 1 kg and half a kilogram (5 tenths). 1,000 g + 500 g = 1,500 g.

items.q: Which mass is the greatest?
items.e: Change all to grams: 1 kg 300 g = 1,300 g. 1,300 g is more than 1,030 g, 1,003 g and 130 g.

items.q: Order from lightest to heaviest: 2 kg, 1,800 g, 700 g
items.e: 2 kg = 2,000 g. So 700 g < 1,800 g < 2,000 g. The 2 kg is the heaviest even though 2 is the smallest number.

items.q: The pan balance is level. What is the mass of the pumpkin?
items.e: 500 g + 500 g = 1,000 g = 1 kg. Then 2 kg + 1 kg = 3 kg. Do not just add the numbers 2 + 500 + 500: they are in different units.

items.q: How many 250 g packs of butter make 1 kg?
Which holds more: 4 L or 4,500 mL?
items.e: 4 L = 4,000 mL. 4,500 mL is more than 4,000 mL.

items.q: Which fact about capacity is true?
items.e: Milli means one thousandth, so 1,000 millilitres make 1 litre.

items.q: A teaspoon holds about how much?
items.e: A teaspoon is a good benchmark for 5 mL. 500 mL is half of a 1 L carton of milk.

items.q: Half of a litre is how many millilitres?
items.e: 1 L = 1,000 mL. Half of 1,000 is 500, so half a litre is 500 mL.

items.q: 3 L = ☐ mL
Which holds more: 2 L or 1,900 mL?
items.e: 2 L = 2,000 mL. 2,000 mL is more than 1,900 mL, so 2 L is more. Compare in the same unit.

items.q: A 1 L carton of milk has a mass of about how much?
items.e: 1 L of milk or water has a mass of about 1 kg. So a 1 L carton is a benchmark for 1 kg.
1,000 mL = 1 L, so 4,000 mL is 4 groups of 1,000 mL: 4 L.

items.q: 6 L = ☐ mL
10 L = ☐ mL
1 L 250 mL = ☐ mL
4 L 80 mL = ☐ mL
items.e: 4 L = 4,000 mL. Add the 80 mL: 4,000 + 80 = 4,080 mL. Keep the 0 in the hundreds place.
2.5 L is 2 L and half a litre (5 tenths). 2,000 mL + 500 mL = 2,500 mL.

items.q: Which capacity is the greatest?
items.e: Change all to millilitres: 2 L 50 mL = 2,050 mL and 2 L 5 mL = 2,005 mL. 2,500 mL is the greatest.

items.q: Order from least to most: 1 L, 300 mL, 1,100 mL
How many 250 mL glasses can you fill from a full 1 L jug?
items.e: 1 L = 1,000 mL. Count by 250: 250, 500, 750, 1,000. That is 4 glasses.

items.q: Gauri empties a full 1 L jug into the tall vase A. It fills up, and 400 mL is left in the jug. Then she empties another full 1 L jug into the short bowl B. It fills up, and 100 mL is left. Which container holds more?
items.e: Vase A holds 1,000 − 400 = 600 mL. Bowl B holds 1,000 − 100 = 900 mL. The bowl holds more. A taller container does not always hold more.

items.q: How many grams are in 1 kilogram?
items.e: Kilo means 1,000, so 1 kg = 1,000 g.

items.q: How many millilitres are in 1 litre?
items.e: Milli means one thousandth, so 1 L = 1,000 mL.

items.q: About what is the mass of a bag of sugar?
items.e: A bag of sugar is about 1 kilogram (1,000 g). 1 g is about the mass of a paper clip.

items.q: About how much does a teaspoon hold?
items.e: A teaspoon holds about 5 millilitres. 500 mL is about a big bottle of water.

items.q: About how much does a can of fizzy drink hold?
items.e: A can of drink holds about 330 millilitres, which is about one third of a litre.

items.q: Convert. 5 kg = ☐ g
items.e: 1 kg = 1,000 g. Kilograms are bigger than grams, so you need more grams: multiply. 5 × 1,000 = 5,000, so 5 kg = 5,000 g.

items.q: Convert. 6 L = ☐ ml
items.e: 1 L = 1,000 mL. Litres are bigger than millilitres, so you need more millilitres: multiply. 6 × 1,000 = 6,000, so 6 L = 6,000 mL.

items.q: Convert. 3,000 g = ☐ kg
items.e: 1 kg = 1,000 g. Kilograms are bigger than grams, so you need fewer kilograms: divide. 3,000 ÷ 1,000 = 3, so 3,000 g = 3 kg.

items.q: Convert. 7,000 mL = ☐ l
items.e: 1 L = 1,000 mL. Litres are bigger than millilitres, so you need fewer litres: divide. 7,000 ÷ 1,000 = 7, so 7,000 mL = 7 L.

items.q: Convert. 2 kg 300 g = ☐ g
Which is the heaviest?
items.e: Change them all to grams: 1 kg 500 g = 1,500 g and 1 kg 50 g = 1,050 g. 1,500 g is the most. Do not compare only the numbers 1 and 1,450.

items.q: Which is the longest?
items.e: Change them all to centimetres: 1 m 20 cm = 120 cm and 1 m 5 cm = 105 cm. 150 cm is the longest.

items.q: Which holds the most?
items.e: Change them all to millilitres: 1 L 250 mL = 1,250 mL and 1 L 50 mL = 1,050 mL. 1,500 mL is the most.
Each mark is 1,000 ÷ 4 = 250 g. A shows 2 kg 750 g and B shows 3 kg 250 g. B is heavier. From 2 kg 750 g to 3 kg is 250 g, and to 3 kg 250 g is 250 g more: 500 g.

items.q: Which list goes from the coldest to the warmest?
items.e: Below zero is colder than 0 °C. −2 °C is the coldest, then 0 °C, then 3 °C.

items.q: At the swimming carnival, Gauri’s stopwatch shows 00:58. Varun’s stopwatch shows 01:02. Who is faster, and by how much?
items.e: 00:58 is 58 s. 01:02 is 1 min 2 s = 62 s. The smaller time is faster, so Gauri wins. 62 − 58 = 4 s.

items.q: Mother stands on the bathroom scales: 62 kg. Then she picks up the dog and the scales show 71 kg. What is the mass of the dog?
items.e: The dog’s mass is the difference: 71 − 62 = 9 kg.

items.q: The school canteen buys 2 kg 500 g of onions for the sausage sizzle. They use 1 kg 750 g. How much is left?
items.e: Change to grams: 2,500 − 1,750 = 750 g. Do not take 500 from 750: the grams part needs regrouping.

items.q: A jug holds 1 L 500 mL of cordial. Six cups of 200 mL are poured for a picnic. How much cordial is left in the jug?
At the athletics carnival, Dev jumps 2 m 45 cm and Tara jumps 2 m 70 cm. How much further does Tara jump?
items.e: The metres are the same, so compare the centimetres: 70 − 45 = 25 cm.
